lead.headline: Israel's election ends with no majority as Netanyahu bloc leads count
lead.dek: With 72% counted, Netanyahu's bloc holds 54 seats and Eisenkot's 48; final results are due Friday
body: Israel's election produced no governing majority, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc leading Wednesday's partial count but short of the 61 Knesset seats needed to govern, and the opposition bloc of former military chief Gadi Eisenkot also falling short.

With about 72% of ballots counted by the Central Elections Committee, Netanyahu's bloc held 54 seats, Eisenkot's alliance 48 and the Arab parties 18, Al Jazeera reported. Official data cited by CBS News at the 60% mark gave Likud 21.4% of the vote and Eisenkot's Yashar party 16.2%. Turnout reached 77.7%, the highest since 1999.

Netanyahu called for a "national right-wing government" and ruled out a coalition with Arab parties; Eisenkot said voters had chosen change. Final results are due by Friday, after which President Isaac Herzog nominates a candidate who gets up to 42 days to form a government. If none forms, Israel faces its sixth election since 2019.

briefs.headline: Grand jury declines to indict Jan. 6 witness Cassidy Hutchinson
briefs.summary: A Washington grand jury refused to indict the former White House aide over her 2022 testimony about Trump's conduct on Jan. 6, AP and CBS News reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

briefs.headline: Hackers knock FEC filing system offline before midterms
briefs.summary: The electronic filing system has been down since late Monday, Reuters reported, citing an FEC email; campaigns cannot file 24- and 48-hour spending reports a week before Election Day.

briefs.headline: New Mexico flood damage may reach $300M as more rain looms
briefs.summary: At least two people died in New Mexico and 200 to 300 were rescued in San Juan County; the $300M figure is the governor's estimate, and the weather service expects more rain Friday night.

briefs.headline: Iran war has cost U.S. military at least $47.1B, estimate says
briefs.summary: A Central Command estimate obtained by CBS News counts $29B for munitions and $6.1B for lost equipment; Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth put the cost at $37.5B three months ago.

briefs.headline: Two high-speed trains collide in Spain, killing at least 10
briefs.summary: A Renfe train ran into an Iryo train near Urda in Toledo province Wednesday morning; Spain's state news agency put the early toll at 10 or more.

briefs.headline: Cyclone Arnab makes landfall in Andhra Pradesh
briefs.summary: The storm came ashore between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam with winds of 125 to 135 km/h, India's weather department said; nearly 100,000 people were evacuated in two states.

briefs.headline: Flavio Bolsonaro leaves Brazil after runoff defeat
briefs.summary: Argentina's migration agency said he flew on to Guayaquil, Ecuador, Tuesday night; a U.S. State Department official said his family will get visas.

briefs.headline: Toll from Nigeria village attack rises to 62
briefs.summary: Nigeria's emergency agency said at least 62 people died when gunmen attacked Binnari village in Taraba state on Friday; police said Tuesday the toll could rise.

briefs.headline: WVU police search two fraternity houses in hazing inquiry
briefs.summary: Officers served warrants Monday night at the Lambda Chi Alpha and Pi Kappa Alpha houses in Morgantown; WVU had suspended Lambda Chi on Oct. 9. No arrests were reported.

briefs.headline: Kanawha prosecutor asks to step aside in ambulance death case
briefs.summary: Debra Rusnak filed Monday to be removed from the case of a former ambulance driver charged in John Lucas' April death, citing threats and confrontations.

briefs.headline: Judge to hear challenge to AG's probe of environmental groups
briefs.summary: WV Rivers Coalition and 350.org ask Judge Joseph Goodwin on Thursday to block J.B. McCuskey's consumer-protection subpoenas seeking 10 years of records.

briefs.headline: Hope Scholarship awards climb 37.6% to 14,486 students
briefs.summary: Monday's annual report shows $75 million moved to student accounts in 2025-26, with Kanawha County leading at 1,688 recipients.

regional.item: Huntington City Council approved a $182,607 contract Monday for a slip repair on 5th Avenue in Guyandotte.
Eric Richmond, charged with murder in the April shooting of a worker outside the Nitro Walmart, will stand trial April 5, 2027.
Parkersburg City Council voted 5-3 on first reading Tuesday to raise the mayor's salary from $90,000 to $125,000.
New River Gorge National Park will close Cunard Road from Nov. 9 and Glade Creek Road from Nov. 10 through March 25 for roadwork.

away.item: Bennington's Select Board voted Monday to join Pownal and Shaftsbury in studying a union municipal district for EMS.

hotspots.item: The Webster County FRN's five-year, $1.25M Drug Free Communities grant, announced Oct. 15, has the Haven Coalition hiring a project coordinator.
Surf City named Jason Casteen its next police chief in a town notice posted Oct. 20, ahead of Chief Nas's Nov. 6 last day.

briefs.headline: Prince George 911 centre switches to digital system Thursday
briefs.summary: The RCMP North District communications centre moves to Next Generation 911 on Oct. 29; it answers calls from about 40 communities, Haida Gwaii to the Alberta border.

briefs.headline: B.C. NDP caucus to pick interim leader this week
briefs.summary: The caucus said Tuesday it would review the campaign and set a timeline for a leadership race; preliminary results have the NDP leading in 28 ridings, down from 47.

briefs.headline: Rejected ballots jump to 303 in Peace River North
briefs.summary: Initial results show 2.82% of votes in the Fort St. John riding were rejected, up from 18 in 2024; a UNBC lecturer called them likely protest votes after the NDP and Greens sat out.

briefs.headline: Ottawa tables MAID bill barring mental illness as sole basis
briefs.summary: Bill C-41 would amend the Criminal Code to exclude mental illness alone and allow advance requests, but only in provinces that legislate their own safeguards.

briefs.headline: EU officials pitch ties 'closer to membership' before Montreal summit
briefs.summary: Canada hosts the EU in Montreal this week; officials speaking on background in Brussels said the bloc wants the closest possible association and deals on trade, security and technology.

briefs.headline: Rubin Observatory turns up candidate dwarf planet beyond Neptune
briefs.summary: Astronomers using Vera C. Rubin Observatory data found 2026 ED138, an object 600 to 1,500 km across about 46 au from the Sun, the largest trans-Neptunian find in about 20 years if confirmed.

briefs.headline: Colorectal cancer rates rise across nearly all age groups
briefs.summary: A University of Chicago study in NEJM Evidence finds U.S. incidence climbed to 38.3 per 100,000 in 2023 after two decades of decline, with the steepest rise, 12.76% a year, in ages 45 to 49.

briefs.headline: Rice team flash-heats e-waste to recover 90% of its antimony
briefs.summary: Rice University chemists report in Nature Chemical Engineering that millisecond Joule heating pulls about 90% of antimony from flame-retardant plastics and captures 83% of the bromide as gas.

briefs.headline: NASA crew exits 378-day Mars simulation on Saturday
briefs.summary: The four-member CHAPEA Mission 2 crew leaves NASA's 3D-printed habitat at Johnson Space Center in Houston on Oct. 31, after 378 days of isolation that began Oct. 19, 2025.

briefs.headline: AI agent finds 4 severe flaws in industrial control software
briefs.summary: Causal Security says its autonomous agent Cipher found and validated four exploitable bugs in the open-source EPICS control toolkit, one rated critical, in under four hours; CISA issued an advisory.

briefs.headline: OpenAI asks outside experts to check AI proofs in math, physics
briefs.summary: OpenAI says internal models produced proofs refuting the Exponential Time Hypothesis and settling a 1991 conjecture; Ryan Williams, Russell Impagliazzo and Nobel laureate David Gross lead unpaid reviews.

briefs.headline: Chatbots fail to spot other chatbots in reverse Turing tests
briefs.summary: Paris Cite University researchers ran 238 tests with seven large language models as judges; AI partners given a structured prompt were never identified, while 88% of humans were.
